Classic gems, tasteful customs, legendary supercars - for Silvian, they're all fair game. He's been in love with cars and motorcycles for as long as he can remember, so it made perfect sense to eventually turn that passion into a full-time writing career. Around six years and more than 3,000 articles later, he is still going strong and doesn't plan on hitting the brakes anytime soon.
It goes without saying that a hypercar as extreme as the upcoming Bugatti Tourbillon requires extensive real-world testing in different environments. The thermal and mechanical stress endured by that 1,800-hp V16 hybrid powertrain is enormous, and extreme climates will exacerbate that strain to the point where components start giving out.
To make sure this doesn’t happen, the Tourbillon is being put to the test in some of the harshest conditions mother nature has to offer. So far, it withstood Dubai’s searing heat at temperatures exceeding 122°F and, at the other extreme, Sweden’s brutal winter in -22°F weather. And Bugatti isn’t done with its fire and ice trials just yet, so the Tourbillon found itself testing under the scorching sun yet again.
Hellish Heat Is Nothing For The Next Bugatti Hypercar
Southern Spain served as its proving ground on this occasion, where the Tourbillon had temperatures well above 104° to contend with. The idea was to see how its intricate cooling system and climate control would hold up when the Bugatti is pushed hard on the racetrack, while noting what needs to be improved on its path toward top-notch refinement.
“We are delivering cars all over the world,” said vehicle development engineer Daniel Ríos Hidalgo. “We have customers from lots of places that are going to drive the cars in different conditions. We need to make sure that these cars perform properly in all these varieties of conditions.” And although performance is Bugatti’s number-one priority, comfort inside the cabin can’t be anything less than exceptional.
What’s The Next Chapter Of The Tourbillon Saga?
Bugatti’s press release didn’t specify if more testing is scheduled to take place, but we do know that Tourbillon deliveries will start this year. Production is rumored to have started last month, and the entire 250-unit run has long been sold out. The brand will build approximately 80 cars per year at its newly inaugurated La Manufacture facility in Molsheim, with the last of them expected to reach its owner in 2029.
If any were still available, you’d need a cool €3.8 million ($4.26 million) before taxes to get your hands on one. No big deal; only twice as much as the average American makes in a lifetime. And with that kind of price tag, it makes perfect sense why Bugatti wants to iron out every possible crease.
CarBuzz Insight – Why This Matters:
Our anticipation is high every time Bugatti releases a new model, and the Tourbillon is no different. It represents a major shift toward a new era, which does away with the W16 engine layout while replacing forced induction with hybridization. This alone sets it apart from anything that came before it.
And given the car’s new powertrain configuration, real-world tests like the one recently performed in Spain are crucial to its development. Even if it uses fewer radiators than the quad-turbo Veyron and Chiron (eight instead of 10), a cooling system this intricate requires a lot of fine-tuning to make sure everything works exactly as intended. Clearly aware of this, Bugatti seems to have done its homework.

SIP contributions reached a fresh record in September, even as the mutual fund industry's overall assets declined.
October 12, 2026 / 13:25 IST
Representative Image: Monthly SIP contributions reached a record Rs 32,490 crore in September 2026, rising from Rs 32,297 crore in August.
Monthly systematic investment plan (SIP) contributions reached a fresh all-time high of Rs 32,490 crore in September 2026, continuing their upward trend even as the overall assets managed by India's mutual fund industry declined during the month.
According to the latest data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI), SIP contributions increased from Rs 32,297 crore in August, a rise of Rs 193 crore, or around 0.6 percent.

The latest figure marks another monthly high for SIP contributions, which had crossed Rs 32,000 crore for the first time in August.
SIP assets stand at Rs 17.86 lakh crore
During September, around 63 lakh new SIPs were registered, according to AMFI data.
The total assets under management (AUM) through SIPs stood at Rs 17.86 lakh crore at the end of September.
SIPs allow investors to invest a fixed amount in mutual fund schemes at regular intervals, usually every month, rather than investing a large amount at once.
Monthly SIP contributions represent the money invested through these plans during a particular month, while SIP AUM reflects the value of investments held through SIPs.
The September data shows that monthly SIP contributions continued to rise, although the pace of increase from August was relatively modest.
Overall mutual fund assets decline
While SIP contributions reached a new high, the mutual fund industry's overall net assets under management declined during September.
Total industry AUM stood at Rs 82.64 lakh crore as of September 30, compared with Rs 87.08 lakh crore at the end of August, a decline of around 5.1 percent.
The fall came as debt mutual funds recorded net outflows of Rs 1.83 lakh crore during September.
Equity-oriented mutual funds, meanwhile, attracted Rs 38,306.55 crore, up nearly 31 percent from Rs 29,328.62 crore in August.
Within equity schemes, small-cap funds received Rs 9,038.57 crore, followed by mid-cap funds at Rs 7,834.84 crore and flexi-cap funds at Rs 6,701.80 crore.
The contrasting numbers show that SIP contributions can continue to rise even when the industry's overall assets decline, as AUM is also affected by redemptions and changes in the market value of investments.

articles.title: Steam hits new all-time high of over 43 million concurrent users just 7 months after its last record as Wardogs and Deadlock surge in popularity - GamesRadar+

articles.full_text:
We regularly report on individual games breaking their concurrent player records on Steam, but this time the focus is on Valve's storefront itself. This month, October 2026, the marketplace hit a new all-time record for concurrent users, safely leapfrogging the previous benchmark.
Per SteamDB, Valve's platform had a ridiculous 43,505,724 people using it at once during October 11. That's a significant amount of accounts to be active at once, to say the least.
The last record, a similarly beefy 42,686,616, wasn't actually that long ago, occurring in March of this year. 2026 is turning out to be a good lap around the sun for Gabe Newell and his cohorts. I'm sure he'll be buying more yachts to celebrate.
Latest Videos FromGamesRadar+
For comparison, the current number is more than the last recorded populations of Canada, Poland, and Mozambique. I'd joke about Valve founding its own sovereign state using fans of Steam, but I wouldn't put it past them to do it for a meme.
The service has enjoyed an increased uptick this decade compared to the last. Starting with a surge while we were all in lockdown, Steam crossed the 40 million threshold a good deal quicker than it did the 20 million line.
Even without hard data, there are accelerants we can point towards here. The diversity of games available, since Steam offers a huge amount of indie and lower-specced releases alongside all the triple-A stuff, and more live-service projects such as Wardogs and Deadlock that start off in early access or are simply preferable on PC.
But mostly I think this just makes it clear more people than ever are enjoying video games in some form or another. Which is great for everyone, but especially those of us who're still hoping for Half-Life 3. Someday, comrades.
Steam on track to earn a record $20 billion this year thanks to games like The Witcher 3 Remastered and Wardogs, analyst says after a massive September.

Heavy rain batters Delhi-NCR, IMD issues red alert; flight ops remain normal
The red alert is currently in place for all 11 districts of Delhi, with the weather department forecasting thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds of up to 60 kmph and heavy rainfall exceeding 15 mm per hour.

Several parts of Delhi were flooded as a result of the heavy rain. (PTI Photo)
Delhi woke up to heavy rain and thunderstorms on Monday as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert, warning of moderate to heavy rainfall across the National Capital Region (NCR). Flight operations at the Delhi airport, however, remained normal despite the spell of intense weather.
A western disturbance has impacted weather conditions across northern India, contributing to the change in weather. The system has triggered unsettled conditions, with rainfall and thunderstorms affecting parts of the region.
#WATCH | Delhi: Rain lashes parts of the National Capital. Visuals from the Rajokri area. https://t.co/dwpu0L0K6k— ANI (@ANI) October 12, 2026
The red alert is currently in place for all 11 districts of Delhi, with the weather department forecasting thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds of up to 60 kmph and heavy rainfall exceeding 15 mm per hour until 9 am.
An orange alert was also issued for Haryana's Faridabad, Gurugram, Rohtak and Sonipat, as well as nine districts in Uttar Pradesh, warning of thunderstorms, lightning, winds gusting at 40-60 kmph and moderate to intense rainfall.
Meanwhile, the Delhi airport said flight operations were running normally despite the possibility of adverse weather conditions.
In a post on X, the airport said ground teams were coordinating with all stakeholders to minimise disruptions and ensure a smooth journey for passengers. Travellers were advised to contact their respective airlines for the latest flight updates.
The rainfall brought some relief from the recent warm conditions, with cloudy skies and showers keeping the region cooler. As a result of the rain, the temperature has dropped by 1-2 degrees.
The downpour wreaked havoc in parts of the capital, leaving roads waterlogged near Jhandewalan Temple in Karol Bagh. Several other parts of the city also bore the brunt of the intense spell, with uprooted trees and flooding adding to the disruption.
The IMD had also cautioned commuters about possible traffic delays, a higher risk of road accidents and water accumulation on roads and in low-lying areas following the rainfall.
It advised people to check traffic conditions before setting out, follow official traffic advisories and steer clear of stretches prone to waterlogging.
Despite the change in weather, daytime temperatures in Delhi are expected to hover between 31 and 35 degrees Celsius over the next few days, according to the IMD.
In its seven-day forecast issued on Sunday evening, the IMD predicted dry weather and partly cloudy skies from Tuesday to Saturday.

Delhi woke up to heavy rain and thunderstorms on Monday morning, bringing cooler conditions across the national capital and the wider NCR region. The showers led to waterlogging in several areas, with the Monday morning rush expected to add to traffic congestion at key choke points.
Similar weather conditions were reported in Noida, Gurugram and Ghaziabad as rain swept across Delhi-NCR.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for the national capital, warning of heavy rainfall exceeding 15 mm per hour and severe thunderstorms with wind gusts of 60 kmph. The nowcast warning was issued at 6 am on Monday and is valid until 9 am, indicating the possibility of intense rain and strong winds in the area.
Waterlogging in parts of Delhi
Heavy rainfall triggered waterlogging near Jhandewalan Temple in the Karol Bagh area of central Delhi. The showers, coinciding with the morning commute, raised the likelihood of traffic disruptions across the region.
The IMD had warned of minor traffic disruptions, a higher risk of vehicle accidents and water accumulation on roads and in low-lying areas for October 11. It advised commuters to check traffic conditions before leaving, follow traffic advisories and avoid stretches prone to waterlogging.
Delhi weather: No rain likely over next six days
Despite the early-morning showers, the IMD has forecast partly cloudy skies and no rainfall in Delhi over the next six days. Maximum temperatures are expected to remain between 31 and 35 degrees Celsius during the coming days.
According to the weather department's seven-day forecast issued on Sunday evening, the maximum temperature on October 13 is likely to range between 32 and 34 degrees Celsius, while the minimum is expected to remain between 23 and 25 degrees Celsius.
On October 14, the maximum temperature is forecast to rise to 33-35 degrees Celsius, with the minimum likely to stay between 23 and 25 degrees Celsius. For October 15, the maximum is expected to range between 31 and 33 degrees Celsius and the minimum between 23 and 25 degrees Celsius.
On October 16 and 17, maximum temperatures are likely to remain between 32 and 34 degrees Celsius, while minimum temperatures are expected to range between 22 and 24 degrees Celsius on both days. Partly cloudy skies and no rainfall are forecast throughout this period

Red alert for heavy rain in several parts of Sri Lanka on Tuesday
October 12, 2026 at
9:11 PM
The Department of Meteorology has issued a heavy rain advisory warning of severe weather conditions affecting several provinces across Sri Lanka, effective until 6:30 p.m. on October 13.
Issued by the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre at 6:30 p.m. on October 12 the bulletin warns that showers or thundershowers will occur across most parts of the island. Under a Red Warning (Take action) risk level, heavy rainfall exceeding 100 mm is likely at some places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa and Southern provinces, as well as in the Kandy and Nuwara-Eliya districts. Meanwhile, an Amber Advisory has been issued for remaining regions depicted under moderate risk.
Residents and authorities in the affected areas are advised to stay alert to potential heavy downpours and associated hazards during the valid period. (Newswire)
